newsitem.title: USA: NYC Independent Budget Office sees bigger revenues.
newsitem.headline: NYC Independent Budget Office sees bigger revenues.

text.p: New York City's Independent Budget Office (IBO) predicted Tuesday the city would take in $266 million more revenues in fiscal 1998 than Mayor Rudolph Giuliani projected in his budget.

IBO, which serves the same role for the city as the Congressional Budget Office does for Washington, said its more optimistic view was based on the assumption that New York City's economy will moderate -- but not until close to the end of the year.

"The difference between our revenue forecast and the mayor's is that since IBO doesn't expect local economic growth to slow until late in this calender year, we are forecasting stronger growth in the city's cyclically-sensitive taxes in the upcoming fiscal year," Douglas Criscitello said in prepared remarks.
IBO predicts the city will get more revenues from several taxes, including ones on personal income, general corporations, unincorporated businesses and general sales.
A Giuliani official was not immediately available to comment on the IBO's analysis of the mayor's budget.

The group also recommended the city take further steps to set-up a Rainy Day fund, though it praised Giuliani for saying he would roll $200 million of an expected 1998 surplus into the following fiscal 1999, which the mayor said would serve as an unofficial short-term stabilization fund. The city's fiscal years start on July 1, and the budget director has said he expected to have a new budget approved around the target date of June 10.

"However, a more formalized rainy day fund would provide a more reliable cushion in the event of an economic downturn," Criscitello said. The City Council has proposed that the city establish an official rainy day fund, a step that would require Albany's approval.
